header.title: Override styles
header.description: Recommended approach to customize @gem-org components in React, Vite and Tailwind projects.

recommendation.title: Don't add styled-components
recommendation.body: In a React + Vite + Tailwind stack, runtime CSS-in-JS adds a second styling system and a cost on every render. The most efficient, current pattern combines three pieces: Tailwind CSS, class-variance-authority (cva) and CSS variables in the style prop.

tailwind.title: Tailwind + cn()
tailwind.body: Structure, layout and one-off tweaks. Override a component's styles through className without conflicts.

cva.title: Variants with cva
cva.body: Define typed variants (intent, size, shape) in one place and reuse them.

cssVars.title: CSS variables
cssVars.body: Runtime-computed values and gem-system token overrides inside a scope.

rows.variants: A component with several fixed looks
rows.dynamic: A value that changes at runtime (color, progress, position)

header.title: Tailwind + cn()
header.description: Tailwind for structure and fast design; clsx + tailwind-merge so className overrides the component without conflicts.

install.title: Step 1 · Install dependencies
install.description: Tailwind v4 with its Vite plugin, plus clsx and tailwind-merge for the cn() utility.

vite.title: Step 2 · Register the Vite plugin
vite.description: The plugin processes Tailwind CSS and only generates the classes it finds in your code.

css.title: Step 3 · Import the utilities
css.description: Import the theme and utilities, without preflight and as important.
css.why: gem-system styles are not inside @layer. In CSS, unlayered rules beat @layer utilities regardless of specificity, so without important your classes would never override the component.
css.preflight: Preflight is Tailwind's global reset: it changes margins, borders and typography on every element and can alter gem-system components.

main.title: Step 4 · Load the CSS in the app
main.description: Import it after the gem-system styles.

cn.title: Step 5 · Create cn()
cn.description: clsx handles conditional classes; tailwind-merge drops conflicting ones and keeps the last.

layout.title: Step 6 · Layout with utilities and tokens
layout.description: Use utilities for structure. Read system tokens with bg-(--gem-color-bg) to follow the light/dark theme.

override.title: Step 7 · Override a component with className
override.description: Classes passed through className apply on top of the component's styles.

wrapper.title: Step 8 · Wrap it in your own component
wrapper.description: Define base classes and let consumers override them with className. cn() makes sure the last one wins.

merge.title: What tailwind-merge solves
merge.description: Live cn() output on this page: classes from the same group are replaced and the rest are kept.

tips.title: Best practices
tips.tokens: Prefer gem-system tokens (bg-(--gem-color-accent)) over fixed Tailwind colors so the theme is respected.
tips.className: Always expose className on your components and pass it last to cn().
tips.important: With utilities imported as important, you don't need the ! modifier on each class.
tips.scope: Use Tailwind for one-off tweaks; when a combination repeats, turn it into a cva variant.

header.title: Variants with cva
header.description: class-variance-authority defines a component's variants in one typed place and returns the className for each combination.

install.title: Step 1 · Install
install.description: cva doesn't depend on Tailwind, but pairs with cn() to resolve conflicts.

anatomy.title: Step 2 · Anatomy of a definition
anatomy.description: Base classes, a variants map and default values.

playground.title: Step 3 · Try the variants
playground.description: Change the props and see which className cva returns.
playground.label: Label

compound.title: Step 4 · compoundVariants
compound.description: Apply classes only when a combination matches. Here, outline + lg uses a thicker border.

types.title: Step 5 · Type with VariantProps
types.description: VariantProps infers props from the definition: adding a variant doesn't require editing types by hand.

matrix.title: Every combination
matrix.description: intent × size from the same definition.

extend.title: Step 6 · Extend gem-system components
extend.description: Add your own variants to a gem-system Button without touching the library: cva builds the className and gem-system keeps the rest.
extend.label: Continue

tips.title: Best practices
tips.single: One cva definition per component, exported next to it.
tips.defaults: Always define defaultVariants so the component works without props.
tips.boolean: For boolean variants use the true / false keys.
tips.cn: Wrap the result with cn() so an external className wins.

header.title: CSS variables
header.description: For runtime-computed values, pass CSS variables through style and consume them from static classes.

why.title: Step 1 · Why not interpolate classes
why.description: Tailwind only generates classes it finds written in code. A class built at runtime doesn't exist in the CSS.

basic.title: Step 2 · Define and consume
basic.description: The value travels in the variable; the class stays static. Here --progress controls the width.
basic.label: Progress

types.title: Step 3 · Type your own variables
types.description: Extend CSSProperties once so you don't have to cast every style.

brand.title: Step 4 · Several variables combined
brand.description: Runtime hue and radius feed static border, background and hover classes.
brand.cardBody: Color and radius come from CSS variables set in style.

scope.title: Step 5 · Override gem-system tokens in a scope
scope.description: gem-system components read --gem-* variables. Redefine them on a container and everything inside changes, without touching the rest of the page.

tips.title: Best practices
tips.prefix: Use your own prefix (--brand-*) to avoid clashing with --gem-*.
tips.units: Pass the unit in the value (12px) or use calc() in the class.
tips.static: If the value is fixed, skip the variable: a class or a cva variant is enough.
tips.scope: To retheme an area, redefine the --gem-* tokens on the container.
